author: Tiana Maxwell
title: Greensboro police urge drivers to use tip line to help crack down on unsafe drivers - NewsBreak
text:
By Tiana Maxwell ,
1 hours ago
GREENSBORO, N.C. (WGHP) — Speeding and reckless driving are at the top of the list of complaints in the Greensboro Police Department's traffic tip line.
Since Jan. 1, the department has conducted 1,202 traffic stops thanks to its traffic tip line.
Those stops led to nearly 900 traffic charges, which include 480 for speeding.
Greensboro Police Department Lt. Calvert works in the Special Operations Division and says the majority of complaints they receive stem from speeding and reckless driving. He says the tip line helps police put eyes on areas of concern.
"We don't know all of the traffic problems," Calvert said. We know where we have historically seen traffic issues with our major thoroughfares, if it's Wendover Avenue, if it's Battleground, if it's the interstate, but we don't know where there are isolated problems."
He said a majority of calls are linked to residential neighborhoods around the city.
"Folks calling in because there's somebody speeding in their neighborhood and they're worried about the safety of kids being out in the street. Things like that," Calvert said.
Steve Gordon has complaints of his own about drivers passing by his home near Wendover Avenue.
"These buzz-bomb mufflers on these small cars, and the large diesel pickup trucks," Gordon said. "The Chargers and the Mustangs ... those are all synthetic noises put on to some extent by the manufacturer and it's all very disturbing."
If there’s an area you want police to check out, call their traffic tip-line at (336) 373-(SLOW) 7569.
"We need you to call it. Again, it's 373-slow," Calvert said.
"Call the number, tell us what's happening and then, hopefully, from there, we get that information, we go out and we're able to make your neighborhood safer."
